newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO-Israeli talks to resume despite Hebron attack.
newsitem.headline: PLO-Israeli talks to resume despite Hebron attack.

text.p: Senior PLO and Israeli officials will meet on Wednesday to try to close a deal on Hebron despite a shooting attack by an Israeli soldier that wounded seven Arabs in the West Bank city, officials said.

Palestinian negotiators and Israeli security sources said Israeli Defense Minister Yitzhak Mordechai was due to hold talks with chief PLO negotiator Mahmoud Abbas at 6:00 p.m. (1600 GMT) at the home of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk.

"The meeting is aimed at trying to finalise the remaining oustanding issues and to prepare for a summit meeting between President (Yasser) Arafat and (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu," said PLO negotiator Jamil al-Tarifi.

An off-duty Israeli soldier sprayed bullets at Palestinian shoppers in a produce market in the heart of Hebron on Wednesday in an attempt to sabotage the imminent handover of 80 percent of the West Bank city to PLO self-rule.

The Hebron handover, due last March, was delayed by a wave of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel ten months ago. It was further pushed off by Netanyahu's demands to bolster safeguards for Jewish settlers in the heart of Hebron.
Hebron, home to 400 Jews and more than 100,000 Arabs, is the last of seven major West Bank cities due to fall under PLO control under a 1995 interim self-rule deal.
The volatile city, holy to Moslems and Jews and a bastion of militancy for both, has long been a flashpoint of violence.
U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross met Netanyahu in Jerusalem and Arafat in Gaza on Wednesday to try to keep negotiations alive.
Netanyahu condemned the shooting and vowed to continue peace talks despite the attack. He said he and Arafat had yet to fix a summit to stich up the Hebron deal.
PLO officials said on Tuesday talks on implementation of the Hebron deal signed last year by the PLO and Israel's previous left-leaning government had been concluded.

They said Mordechai and Abbas were due to discuss oustanding interim issues from the 1995 accord other than Hebron, including fixing dates for further Israeli redeployments from the West Bank and the release of Palestinian prisoners.
"If they conclude tonight, we hope the Arafat-Netanyahu summit will be held on Thursday or Friday," a PLO official said.
